title: Deleting a site gives its Docker network and /24 back to the host, after its SMTP rule and under the allocator lock
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/teardown-volumes.test.mjs

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail' lines and the result of the case named "the site's own network goes with it, and only that one; a network still in use is a teardown that did not finish".
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 19).

The named case is 'ok': after the teardown only the neighbour's network is left, `network rm <label>_default` comes after the subnet's `iptables -C` in the call log, and a network docker refuses to remove is reported with docker's reason, the teardown exits 1 with no success marker saying 'did not finish: the site network <label>_default is still on this host' and keeps its log, and a later teardown takes the network once it is free (it used to succeed and leave it; changed by PR #988).
evidence: 05/10/2026 on the dev Mac stand: 183 `<label>_default` networks, 182 of the 256 /24 subnets under 10.240.0.0/16 taken, most with no container; every test site deleted through the delete door left its network.
fence: teardown removes exactly `<label>_default` once the stack, lane containers, volumes and the subnet's SMTP rule are gone, under the lock provision allocates under; a network in use is reported and left, and the teardown fails so it is run again.

tests: the site's own network goes with it, and only that one; a network still in use is a teardown that did not finish
